name: Somaiya BeliefSat-0
institute: K. J. Somaiya Institute of Technology (KJSIT), Sion, Mumbai
team: New Leap Labs / student satellite team

orbit.note: Near-equatorial low LEO — short orbital lifetime, high drag sensitivity.

purpose: Global amateur-radio (HAM) communications, commemorating 100 years of amateur radio in India and filling the gap left by ISRO HAMSAT (decommissioned 2014/2016).

decay.reason: The ~350 km POEM orbit decays quickly. BeliefSat-0 is no longer in the live catalog — OrbitWatch keeps the mission story and points you at active stations / amateur satellites as analogs.

similarPreset.label: Show similar active objects
similarPreset.hint: Stations + amateur-radio sats occupy the same LEO regime BeliefSat-0 flew in.

timeline.title: Touch the Jovian Moon
timeline.body: KJSIT students win ISRO's competition — the spark for a campus satellite programme.

timeline.title: New Leap begins
timeline.body: Work starts on an amateur-radio satellite and a campus ground station.

timeline.title: PSLV-C58 / POEM
timeline.body: BeliefSat-0 lifts off from Sriharikota as a POEM payload. HAM operators worldwide can activate UHF/VHF services once the experiment module is live.

timeline.title: On-orbit copy
timeline.body: The team reports successful reception of telemetry after launch — 30-second APRS-style beacons designed so students can decode space tech with a modest station.

timeline.title: Re-entry
timeline.body: Catalog decay recorded. The mission is complete; OrbitWatch preserves the story beside live LEO traffic.

groundSegment.note: Pass predictions (N2YO) are a phase-2 add-on. v1 estimates 'above campus horizon' from SGP4 look angles.
